purpose: set up encrypted connections correctly, so traffic is protected and clients can trust the server, with certificates issued and renewed without manual steps
entry_criteria: Hostnames and traffic paths are listed
A certificate authority or automated issuer is chosen
DNS control for the names exists
inputs: termination points in the traffic path
security baseline for protocols and ciphers
procedure: Decide where TLS terminates and whether traffic is re-encrypted to the backend; encrypt internal hops that carry sensitive data.
Issue certificates with the correct names (including alternative names) from the chosen authority, using automated issuance such as ACME.
Configure TLS 1.2 minimum with TLS 1.3 preferred, strong cipher suites, forward secrecy and OCSP stapling, and disable older protocols.
Add HTTP to HTTPS redirect and HSTS, first with a short max-age, then lengthen it once verified.
Protect private keys: restricted access, no copies in repositories, and rotation on staff or compromise events.
Test with an external scanner and from several clients, and record the grade and the expiry dates.
acceptance_criteria: Only supported protocol versions are enabled
Private keys are not in repositories

validation.command: openssl s_client -connect app.example.com:443 -servername app.example.com </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -dates -ext subjectAltName   # example
validation.expect: names and dates are as expected

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A public site terminates TLS 1.3 at the load balancer with an automatically issued certificate, redirects HTTP, sets HSTS at one day then a year after verification, and an external scan shows no legacy protocols.
